blocks.prompt: 4 (i) Sum to \(n\) terms the following series: \(1 \cdot 2 + 3 \cdot 4 + 5 \cdot 8 + 7 \cdot 16 + \cdots\)
blocks.explanation:
This is an A.G.P.: each term is (an A.P. number) \(\times\) (a G.P. number). No formula to memorise; we use multiply-by-\(r\)-and-subtract.
A.P. part \(1, 3, 5, 7, \ldots\); G.P. part \(2, 4, 8, 16, \ldots\) with \(r = 2\).
Plan: find \(T_n\), write \(S_n\) and \(2S_n\) shifted, subtract, sum the G.P. in the middle, solve for \(S_n\).
steps:
Given: \(1 \cdot 2 + 3 \cdot 4 + 5 \cdot 8 + \cdots\); A.P. \(a = 1, d = 2\); G.P. \(b = 2, r = 2\)
To find: \(S_n\), the sum of \(n\) terms.
Method: Multiply-by-\(r\)-and-subtract (the method of 6.8.1): write \(S_n\), write \(rS_n\) one place to the right, subtract; the middle becomes a G.P. that we can sum.

The \(n\)th term
\[a_n = 1 + (n - 1)2 = 2n - 1\]
\[b_n = 2 \cdot 2^{n-1} = 2^{n}\]
\[T_n = (2n - 1)2^{n}\]
Why: A.P. and G.P. \(n\)th terms, multiplied; \(2 \cdot 2^{n-1} = 2^{n}\).

Write \(S_n\) and \(2S_n\)
\[S_n = 1 \cdot 2 + 3 \cdot 2^{2} + 5 \cdot 2^{3}\]
\[\quad + \cdots + (2n - 1)2^{n}\]
\[2S_n = 1 \cdot 2^{2} + 3 \cdot 2^{3} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + (2n - 3)2^{n} + (2n - 1)2^{n+1}\]
Why: Multiplying by \(r = 2\) raises every power of 2 by one, so each term of \(2S_n\) stands under the term of \(S_n\) with the same power.

Subtract \(2S_n\) from \(S_n\)
\[-S_n = 1 \cdot 2 + 2 \cdot 2^{2} + 2 \cdot 2^{3}\]
\[\quad + \cdots + 2 \cdot 2^{n} - (2n - 1)2^{n+1}\]
\[-S_n = 2 + 2(2^{2} + 2^{3} + \cdots + 2^{n})\]
\[\quad - (2n - 1)2^{n+1}\]
Why: Same powers subtract: \((3 - 1)2^2 = 2 \cdot 2^2\), \((5 - 3)2^3 = 2 \cdot 2^3\), and so on (the gap is \(d = 2\)). The first term has nothing under it; the last term of \(2S_n\) has nothing above it.

Sum the G.P. in the bracket
\[2^{2} + 2^{3} + \cdots + 2^{n}\]
\[= \dfrac{4(2^{n-1} - 1)}{2 - 1}\]
\[= 2^{n+1} - 4\]
Why: First term 4, ratio 2, powers 2 to \(n\), so \(n - 1\) terms; \(4 \cdot 2^{n-1} = 2^{n+1}\).

blocks.prompt: 4 (ii) Sum to \(n\) terms the following series: \(2 \cdot 3 + 4 \cdot 3^{2} + 6 \cdot 3^{3} + 8 \cdot 3^{4} + \cdots\)
blocks.explanation:
This is an A.G.P.: each term is (an A.P. number) \(\times\) (a G.P. number). No formula to memorise; we use multiply-by-\(r\)-and-subtract.
A.P. part \(2, 4, 6, 8, \ldots\); G.P. part \(3, 3^2, 3^3, \ldots\) with \(r = 3\).
Plan: find \(T_n\), write \(S_n\) and \(3S_n\) shifted, subtract, sum the G.P., solve for \(S_n\).
steps:
Given: \(2 \cdot 3 + 4 \cdot 3^2 + 6 \cdot 3^3 + \cdots\); A.P. \(a = 2, d = 2\); G.P. \(b = 3, r = 3\)
To find: \(S_n\).
Method: Multiply-by-\(r\)-and-subtract (the method of 6.8.1): write \(S_n\), write \(rS_n\) one place to the right, subtract; the middle becomes a G.P. that we can sum.

The \(n\)th term
\[T_n = 2n \cdot 3^{n}\]
Why: A.P. \(n\)th term \(2 + (n - 1)2 = 2n\); G.P. \(n\)th term \(3 \cdot 3^{n-1} = 3^n\).

Write \(S_n\) and \(3S_n\)
\[S_n = 2 \cdot 3 + 4 \cdot 3^{2} + 6 \cdot 3^{3}\]
\[\quad + \cdots + 2n \cdot 3^{n}\]
\[3S_n = 2 \cdot 3^{2} + 4 \cdot 3^{3} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + (2n - 2)3^{n} + 2n \cdot 3^{n+1}\]
Why: Multiplying by \(r = 3\) raises every power of 3 by one; shift one place so equal powers line up.

Subtract
\[-2S_n = 2 \cdot 3 + 2 \cdot 3^{2} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + 2 \cdot 3^{n} - 2n \cdot 3^{n+1}\]
\[-2S_n = 2(3 + 3^{2} + \cdots + 3^{n})\]
\[\quad - 2n \cdot 3^{n+1}\]
Why: \(S_n - 3S_n = -2S_n\); every matching pair leaves \(d = 2\) times the power; here even the first term \(2 \cdot 3\) fits the pattern.

Sum the G.P.
\[3 + 3^{2} + \cdots + 3^{n}\]
\[= \dfrac{3(3^{n} - 1)}{3 - 1}\]
\[= \dfrac{3^{n+1} - 3}{2}\]
Why: First term 3, ratio 3, \(n\) terms (powers 1 to \(n\)).

Solve for \(S_n\)
\[-2S_n = 3^{n+1} - 3\]
\[\quad - 2n \cdot 3^{n+1}\]
\[S_n = \dfrac{3 + (2n - 1)3^{n+1}}{2}\]
\[= \dfrac{3}{2}[1 + (2n - 1)3^{n}]\]
Why: The 2 in front cancels the 2 below; divide by \(-2\); finally \(3^{n+1} = 3 \cdot 3^n\) lets us take \(\frac{3}{2}\) common.

Match the answer key form
\[n \cdot 3^{n+1} - (n + 1)3^{n}\]
\[= 3n \cdot 3^{n} - (n + 1)3^{n}\]
\[= (2n - 1)3^{n}\]
Why: So the key's \(\frac{3}{2}[1 - (n + 1)3^n + n \cdot 3^{n+1}]\) is the same answer.

blocks.prompt: 4 (iii) Sum to \(n\) terms the following series: \(2 + \frac{5}{4} + \frac{8}{4^{2}} + \frac{11}{4^{3}} + \cdots\)
blocks.explanation:
This is an A.G.P.: each term is (an A.P. number) \(\times\) (a G.P. number). No formula to memorise; we use multiply-by-\(r\)-and-subtract.
A.P. part \(2, 5, 8, 11, \ldots\) (\(a = 2, d = 3\)); the bottoms are powers of 4, so the G.P. part has \(r = \frac{1}{4}\).
Plan: find \(T_n\), write \(S_n\) and \(\frac{1}{4}S_n\) shifted, subtract, sum the G.P., solve for \(S_n\).
steps:
Given: \(2 + \frac{5}{4} + \frac{8}{4^{2}} + \frac{11}{4^{3}} + \cdots\); A.P. part \(2, 5, 8, 11, \ldots\) (\(a = 2, d = 3\)); G.P. part \(b = 1, r = \frac{1}{4}\)
To find: \(S_n\).
Method: Multiply-by-\(r\)-and-subtract (the method of 6.8.1): write \(S_n\), write \(rS_n\) one place to the right, subtract; the middle becomes a G.P. that we can sum.

The \(n\)th term
\[T_n = \dfrac{3n - 1}{4^{n-1}}\]
Why: Top: \(n\)th term of the A.P.; bottom: \(4^{n-1}\) (the first term has \(4^0 = 1\)).

Write \(S_n\) and \(\frac{1}{4}S_n\)
\[S_n = 2 + \dfrac{5}{4} + \dfrac{8}{4^{2}} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{3n - 1}{4^{n-1}}\]
\[\tfrac{1}{4}S_n = \dfrac{2}{4} + \dfrac{5}{4^{2}} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{3n - 4}{4^{n-1}} + \dfrac{3n - 1}{4^{n}}\]
Why: Multiplying by \(\frac{1}{4}\) puts one more 4 in each bottom; shift one place so equal bottoms line up.

Subtract
\[\tfrac{3}{4}S_n = 2 + \dfrac{3}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4^{2}} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{3}{4^{n-1}} - \dfrac{3n - 1}{4^{n}}\]
\[\tfrac{3}{4}S_n = 2 + 3\left(\dfrac{1}{4} + \cdots + \dfrac{1}{4^{n-1}}\right)\]
\[\quad - \dfrac{3n - 1}{4^{n}}\]
Why: \(S_n - \frac{1}{4}S_n = \frac{3}{4}S_n\). Equal bottoms leave \(d\) on top, for example \(\frac{5 - 2}{4} = \frac{3}{4}\); the first term stays and the last term of the second line is subtracted.

Sum the G.P. in the bracket
\[\dfrac{1}{4} + \cdots + \dfrac{1}{4^{n-1}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\frac{1}{4}\left[1 - \left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{n-1}\right]}{1 - \frac{1}{4}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{3}\left[1 - \left(\tfrac{1}{4}\right)^{n-1}\right]\]
Why: First term \(\frac{1}{4}\), ratio \(\frac{1}{4}\), \(n - 1\) terms; use \(\frac{a_1(1 - r^m)}{1 - r}\) since \(r < 1\).

Simplify and solve for \(S_n\)
\[\tfrac{3}{4}S_n = 2 + 1 - \left(\tfrac{1}{4}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[\quad - (3n - 1)\left(\tfrac{1}{4}\right)^{n}\]
\[\tfrac{3}{4}S_n = 3 - \left(\tfrac{1}{4}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[\quad - (3n - 1)\left(\tfrac{1}{4}\right)^{n}\]
\[S_n = 4 - \tfrac{4}{3}\left(\tfrac{1}{4}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[\quad - \tfrac{4}{3}(3n - 1)\left(\tfrac{1}{4}\right)^{n}\]
Why: \(3 \times \frac{1}{3} = 1\) and \(2 + 1 = 3\); then multiply both sides by \(\frac{4}{3}\).

blocks.prompt: 4 (iv) Sum to \(n\) terms the following series: \(1 + \frac{3}{5} + \frac{5}{5^{2}} + \frac{7}{5^{3}} + \cdots\)
blocks.explanation:
This is an A.G.P.: each term is (an A.P. number) \(\times\) (a G.P. number). No formula to memorise; we use multiply-by-\(r\)-and-subtract.
A.P. part \(1, 3, 5, 7, \ldots\) (\(a = 1, d = 2\)); the bottoms are powers of 5, so the G.P. part has \(r = \frac{1}{5}\).
Plan: find \(T_n\), write \(S_n\) and \(\frac{1}{5}S_n\) shifted, subtract, sum the G.P., solve for \(S_n\).
steps:
Given: \(1 + \frac{3}{5} + \frac{5}{5^{2}} + \frac{7}{5^{3}} + \cdots\); A.P. part \(1, 3, 5, 7, \ldots\) (\(a = 1, d = 2\)); G.P. part \(b = 1, r = \frac{1}{5}\)
To find: \(S_n\).
Method: Multiply-by-\(r\)-and-subtract (the method of 6.8.1): write \(S_n\), write \(rS_n\) one place to the right, subtract; the middle becomes a G.P. that we can sum.

The \(n\)th term
\[T_n = \dfrac{2n - 1}{5^{n-1}}\]
Why: Top: \(n\)th term of the A.P.; bottom: \(5^{n-1}\) (the first term has \(5^0 = 1\)).

Write \(S_n\) and \(\frac{1}{5}S_n\)
\[S_n = 1 + \dfrac{3}{5} + \dfrac{5}{5^{2}} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{2n - 1}{5^{n-1}}\]
\[\tfrac{1}{5}S_n = \dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{3}{5^{2}} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{2n - 3}{5^{n-1}} + \dfrac{2n - 1}{5^{n}}\]
Why: Multiplying by \(\frac{1}{5}\) puts one more 5 in each bottom; shift one place so equal bottoms line up.

Subtract
\[\tfrac{4}{5}S_n = 1 + \dfrac{2}{5} + \dfrac{2}{5^{2}} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{2}{5^{n-1}} - \dfrac{2n - 1}{5^{n}}\]
\[\tfrac{4}{5}S_n = 1 + 2\left(\dfrac{1}{5} + \cdots + \dfrac{1}{5^{n-1}}\right)\]
\[\quad - \dfrac{2n - 1}{5^{n}}\]
Why: \(S_n - \frac{1}{5}S_n = \frac{4}{5}S_n\). Equal bottoms leave \(d\) on top, for example \(\frac{3 - 1}{5} = \frac{2}{5}\); the first term stays and the last term of the second line is subtracted.

Sum the G.P. in the bracket
\[\dfrac{1}{5} + \cdots + \dfrac{1}{5^{n-1}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\frac{1}{5}\left[1 - \left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^{n-1}\right]}{1 - \frac{1}{5}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{4}\left[1 - \left(\tfrac{1}{5}\right)^{n-1}\right]\]
Why: First term \(\frac{1}{5}\), ratio \(\frac{1}{5}\), \(n - 1\) terms; use \(\frac{a_1(1 - r^m)}{1 - r}\) since \(r < 1\).

Simplify and solve for \(S_n\)
\[\tfrac{4}{5}S_n = 1 + \tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{1}{2}\left(\tfrac{1}{5}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[\quad - (2n - 1)\left(\tfrac{1}{5}\right)^{n}\]
\[\tfrac{4}{5}S_n = \tfrac{3}{2} - \tfrac{1}{2}\left(\tfrac{1}{5}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[\quad - (2n - 1)\left(\tfrac{1}{5}\right)^{n}\]
\[S_n = \tfrac{15}{8} - \tfrac{5}{8}\left(\tfrac{1}{5}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[\quad - \tfrac{5}{4}(2n - 1)\left(\tfrac{1}{5}\right)^{n}\]
Why: \(2 \times \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{2}\) and \(1 + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{2}\); then multiply both sides by \(\frac{5}{4}\).

blocks.prompt: 4 (v) Sum to \(n\) terms the following series: \(1 + \frac{4}{3} + \frac{7}{9} + \frac{10}{27} + \cdots\)
blocks.explanation:
This is an A.G.P.: each term is (an A.P. number) \(\times\) (a G.P. number). No formula to memorise; we use multiply-by-\(r\)-and-subtract.
A.P. part \(1, 4, 7, 10, \ldots\) (\(a = 1, d = 3\)); the bottoms are powers of 3, so the G.P. part has \(r = \frac{1}{3}\).
Plan: find \(T_n\), write \(S_n\) and \(\frac{1}{3}S_n\) shifted, subtract, sum the G.P., solve for \(S_n\).
steps:
Given: \(1 + \frac{4}{3} + \frac{7}{9} + \frac{10}{27} + \cdots\); A.P. part \(1, 4, 7, 10, \ldots\) (\(a = 1, d = 3\)); G.P. part \(b = 1, r = \frac{1}{3}\)
To find: \(S_n\).
Method: Multiply-by-\(r\)-and-subtract (the method of 6.8.1): write \(S_n\), write \(rS_n\) one place to the right, subtract; the middle becomes a G.P. that we can sum.

The \(n\)th term
\[T_n = \dfrac{3n - 2}{3^{n-1}}\]
Why: Top: \(n\)th term of the A.P.; bottom: \(3^{n-1}\) (the first term has \(3^0 = 1\)).

Write \(S_n\) and \(\frac{1}{3}S_n\)
\[S_n = 1 + \dfrac{4}{3} + \dfrac{7}{3^{2}} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{3n - 2}{3^{n-1}}\]
\[\tfrac{1}{3}S_n = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{4}{3^{2}} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{3n - 5}{3^{n-1}} + \dfrac{3n - 2}{3^{n}}\]
Why: Multiplying by \(\frac{1}{3}\) puts one more 3 in each bottom; shift one place so equal bottoms line up.

Subtract
\[\tfrac{2}{3}S_n = 1 + \dfrac{3}{3} + \dfrac{3}{3^{2}} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + \dfrac{3}{3^{n-1}} - \dfrac{3n - 2}{3^{n}}\]
\[\tfrac{2}{3}S_n = 1 + 3\left(\dfrac{1}{3} + \cdots + \dfrac{1}{3^{n-1}}\right)\]
\[\quad - \dfrac{3n - 2}{3^{n}}\]
Why: \(S_n - \frac{1}{3}S_n = \frac{2}{3}S_n\). Equal bottoms leave \(d\) on top, for example \(\frac{4 - 1}{3} = \frac{3}{3}\); the first term stays and the last term of the second line is subtracted.

Sum the G.P. in the bracket
\[\dfrac{1}{3} + \cdots + \dfrac{1}{3^{n-1}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\frac{1}{3}\left[1 - \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{n-1}\right]}{1 - \frac{1}{3}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\left[1 - \left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{n-1}\right]\]
Why: First term \(\frac{1}{3}\), ratio \(\frac{1}{3}\), \(n - 1\) terms; use \(\frac{a_1(1 - r^m)}{1 - r}\) since \(r < 1\).

Simplify and solve for \(S_n\)
\[\tfrac{2}{3}S_n = 1 + \tfrac{3}{2} - \tfrac{3}{2}\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[\quad - (3n - 2)\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{n}\]
\[\tfrac{2}{3}S_n = \tfrac{5}{2} - \tfrac{3}{2}\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[\quad - (3n - 2)\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{n}\]
\[S_n = \tfrac{15}{4} - \tfrac{9}{4}\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{n-1}\]
\[\quad - \tfrac{3}{2}(3n - 2)\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^{n}\]
Why: \(3 \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{2}\) and \(1 + \frac{3}{2} = \frac{5}{2}\); then multiply both sides by \(\frac{3}{2}\).
